title: BEAST v1.X Tutorial for Bayesian Inference in Cicada Genera
author: Soichi Osozawa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bq6mmzc6
materials: Trees: Tree Prior: Speciation: Yule Process.

steps.title: Install BEAGLE library
steps.instruction: Download and install the BEAGLE Library required for BEAST v1.X before running any BEAST analysis.

steps.title: Prepare sequence files
steps.instruction: Create two plain‑text FASTA files: one for mitochondrial COI (1,534 bp) and one for nuclear 28S rRNA (874 bp). Ensure that each sequence label (e.g., ">kum12") is identical in both files; copy‑paste the labels to keep them coincident.

steps.title: Load data in BEAUti
steps.instruction: Open BEAUti (part of BEAST v1.X, released 10 June 2018) and import the COI and 28S files using the “+” button; each imported sequence will form its own partition.

substeps.instruction: Load taxa as the ingroup also with the “+” button.
In the left Taxon Set panel, check the “Monophyletic” box for all taxa; optionally check the “Stem” box for the kumAll group only.
In the right panel, verify that all taxa appear under “Included Taxa”.

steps.title: Set site substitution models
steps.instruction: For each partition, choose the HKY substitution model, set Base Frequencies to “Empirical”, select the Gamma site‑heterogeneity model with 4 categories, and turn “Partition into codon positions” OFF. (The GTR model yields a similar topology and may be used as an alternative.)

steps.title: Configure clock model
steps.instruction: Select “Uncorrected relaxed clock” as the Clock Type and set the Relaxed Distribution to “Lognormal”. This allows each branch its own rate drawn from a log‑normal distribution.

steps.title: Enter calibration priors
steps.instruction: In the Priors tab, add a Normal distribution for the tMRCA (time of most recent common ancestor) using the calibration points described below:

substeps.instruction: Calibration A (A1‑A6): geological event age 1.55 ± 0.15 Ma (Ryukyu islands).
Calibration B: Hachijo island emergence 0.24 Ma (Izu volcanic arc).
Calibration C: Crown Meimuna opalifera fossil age 6.4 ± 0.4 Ma (Itamuro Formation).
Calibration D: Crown Cryptotympana fossil age 16.45 ± 0.45 Ma (European MN5 stage).
For each point, set the Normal prior’s Mean to the age value and Standard Deviation to the quoted uncertainty.

steps.title: Set MCMC parameters
steps.instruction: In the MCMC tab, set the Length of chain to 10,000,000 steps and keep all other settings at their defaults.

steps.title: Generate XML input file
steps.instruction: Use BEAUti’s “File → Save As” to export the complete analysis configuration as an XML file for BEAST.

steps.title: Run BEAST analysis
steps.instruction: Launch BEAST, load the XML file, and start the run. The analysis will take roughly 3 hours (≈30 min for the small test case, up to 2 h for larger specimen sets).

steps.title: Summarize trees with TreeAnnotator
steps.instruction: After BEAST finishes, open TreeAnnotator, load the BEAST output tree files, and generate a summarized (maximum clade credibility) tree.

steps.title: Visualize annotated tree
steps.instruction: Open the summarized tree in FigTree v1.4.2. Enable display of posterior probability, node ages, and rate median at each node. Export the 95 % highest posterior density intervals if desired.

steps.title: Export rate‑age data (optional)
steps.instruction: Copy the “rate median” and “node age” values from FigTree and plot base‑substitution rate versus age in Excel, if a rate‑through‑time diagram is required.
